extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners; patent practitioners, applicants, and patent attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO/MPEP policy guidance on the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112(a) (pre‑AIA 112, first paragraph), explaining written description, enablement, best mode, and the minimum disclosure quality/quantity needed in a patent specification. Targets how examiners should evaluate specification sufficiency and how applicants should draft disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full and clear description (35 U.S.C. 112(a) / pre‑AIA 112, first paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain a valid patent, a patent application must contain a full and clear description of the invention for which a patent is sought in the manner prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(a) or pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the baseline statutory requirement for the specification; the manual lists detailed subguidance (e.g., sections 2161–2166 and 2163 onward) interpreting how to apply this requirement in examination. The full and clear description obligation underlies written description, enablement, and best mode analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate written description / Demonstration of possession
rubrics_metrics.description: The patentee must disclose sufficient information to demonstrate that the inventor had possession of the invention at the time of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written description requirement ensures the public receives adequate disclosure in exchange for patent rights. See MPEP 2163 et seq. for guidance on the standard for compliance, support for claimed subject matter, typical circumstances where issues arise, burden on examiner, and relationship to claim scope and new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement — disclosure enabling one skilled in the art to make and use the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must disclose sufficient information to enable those skilled in the art to make and use the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enablement is evaluated with respect to the quantity and quality of information needed as of the filing date and may involve analysis of undue experimentation, working/prophetic examples, predictability of the art, and whether the specification is enabling across the full scope of the claims (see MPEP 2164 and subparts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑concealment of best mode
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must not conceal from the public the best way of practicing the invention that was known to the patentee at the time of filing the patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best mode is a separate consideration under the specification requirements; concealment of the best mode known at filing can be a ground for rejecting or invalidating a patent. See MPEP 2165 and related subsections for considerations relevant to best mode and its relation to enablement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum quality and quantity of disclosure required by 35 U.S.C. 112(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 112(a) sets forth the minimum requirements for the quality and quantity of information that must be contained in a patent application to justify the grant of a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle frames both written description and enablement analyses: the disclosure must be sufficiently informative in both quality and quantity to justify excluding the public from practicing the claimed invention during the patent term. The MPEP delineates tests and factors (see 2163–2166) to determine whether the minimum has been met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing the disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to fully comply with the disclosure requirements (written description, enablement, best mode) could result in the denial of a patent, or in a holding of invalidity of an issued patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should apply the written description and enablement standards during prosecution; applicants should ensure their specification supports claim scope, enables practice across claimed scope, and discloses the best mode known. The MPEP provides procedural and substantive guidance on rejections under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and related remedies (see sections 2166, 2164.05, 2165.03, etc.).
